svg.title: An adolescent is admitted with 2 weeks of extreme fatigue, body aches, a low-grade fever and a very sore throat. The tonsils are enlarged with exudate and the cervical lymph nodes are swollen. The abdomen is soft, but the spleen is palpable 3 cm below the costal margin.
svg.desc: Infectious mononucleosis is caused by the Epstein-Barr virus , and the fatigue, sore throat with exudate and swollen nodes all fit. The finding that matters most is the enlarged spleen , because it is fragile and can rupture - which is why contact sports and rough play are avoided for at least 4 weeks. The mononucleosis rapid test (monospot) confirms it. A strep test would be reasonable to rule out, but it does not explain the splenomegaly.
